strategy.summary: Reproduce the cauchy large-|x| defect in scipy.stats: on the buggy commit 49e8876de1fb, cauchy.pdf overflows x**2 for huge |x| and cauchy.logpdf returns -inf for |x| > 1.34e154. Run the two TestCauchy tests added by the PR (test_pdf_no_overflow_warning and test_logpdf) from scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py against a from-source build of the buggy commit and of its fixed child, and expect the transition in those tests. Dependency constraints for NumPy and the _lazywhere helper are both null (unbounded, no era table entry), so the plan uses a current NumPy and the in-tree helper and says so. The PR date is blank, so the era is unknown.

system_packages: gcc or gfortran toolchain able to compile scipy from source
BLAS/LAPACK development libraries (OpenBLAS or the bundled one)
build_commands: pip install --no-build-isolation -e . (or spin build on the buggy commit)
pinned_because: No documented NumPy constraint exists in the evidence (dependency constraint null, era_ceiling null), so NumPy is left unpinned and the choice of a current release is an assumption, not a documented requirement.
No documented constraint exists for the scipy.stats _lazywhere helper; it is in-tree and is built together with scipy, so no separate pin is applied.

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py -k 'TestCauchy and (test_pdf_no_overflow_warning or test_logpdf)' -q -W error::RuntimeWarning
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 49e8876de1fb the test file's new import of _XMAX must resolve, and then test_logpdf fails for every case with |x| above 1.34e154 (logpdf returns -inf where a finite reference is expected, so assert_allclose reports a mismatch), and test_pdf_no_overflow_warning fails only if RuntimeWarning is promoted to an error (the value 0.0 itself already matches, so the warning is the only signal). On the fixed revision both tests pass with rtol 1e-15 and no overflow RuntimeWarning. The transition is the pass/fail change of these tests, not any printed value.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import warnings; warnings.simplefilter('error'); import scipy.stats as s; print(s.cauchy.pdf(1e200)); print(s.cauchy.logpdf(1e200))"  (expect a RuntimeWarning turned error on buggy for pdf, and -inf for logpdf on buggy)
risks: The test file imports _XMAX from scipy.stats._constants. If the buggy commit does not define _XMAX there, the whole module fails at collection with ImportError on the buggy side, so the transition would be an import failure rather than the numerical defect. Check the buggy tree first; if it is missing, substitute np.finfo(np.float64).max for _XMAX (the (_XMAX, -1420.71...) reference is consistent with float max) and state that substitution.

test_pdf_no_overflow_warning passes numerically on the buggy commit because 1/(pi*(1+inf)) is 0.0. It fails on buggy only if the pytest configuration or the -W error flag promotes RuntimeWarning to an error. Without that, only the logpdf tests transition. Do not claim the pdf test transitions by value alone.

The rtol=1e-15 tolerance in test_logpdf is very tight. Reference values come from mpmath, and the fixed implementation's agreement at this tolerance is what makes the pass side hold; a different NumPy or libm version could shift last-bit results and turn an intended pass into a failure. The pass side is not guaranteed on arbitrary platforms.

The defect is an overflow of x**2 in float64. It does not depend on architecture or threading, but results of the fixed f/f2 split could differ on platforms with different libm exp/log or with x87 extended precision, so the pass side is only assured on standard x86_64 or aarch64 Linux builds.
The helper _lazywhere split at absx=1 and at sqrt(float max) is internal and undocumented; the buggy/fixed transition relies on the fixed commit's implementation details, not on a public contract.

No PR date is given, so the era of NumPy and the Python version are unknown; with a much newer NumPy, errstate or warning behaviour on scalar float inputs may differ from the era the test was written for.

Build from source takes significant time and needs a working Fortran/C++ toolchain; a wheel of the release containing the fix cannot substitute for the buggy commit, since the buggy behaviour must come from the tree itself.

oracle.tolerance: rtol=1e-15 via assert_allclose for test_logpdf; exact equality p == 0.0 for test_pdf_no_overflow_warning
oracle.reference_source: mpmath-computed reference values embedded in the test parametrization
oracle.why: test_logpdf compares finite log-densities to mpmath references at rtol 1e-15, and the pdf test uses exact equality to 0.0 at x=1e200.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: For test_logpdf, cases with |x| > 1.34e154 receive -inf from logpdf, and assert_allclose reports a mismatch against the finite reference, so those parametrized cases fail. For test_pdf_no_overflow_warning, the value 0.0 matches, so it fails only if the spurious overflow RuntimeWarning is raised as an error by the -W error flag or pytest filterwarnings configuration.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: Both tests pass: logpdf returns the mpmath reference values to rtol 1e-15 across the full range including _XMAX, and pdf(1e200) returns 0.0 with no overflow RuntimeWarning.
